key_insight: BAGEL is a unified closed-book benchmark that exposes how well large language models understand specialized animal-related knowledge, revealing strengths and specific knowledge gaps across taxa and question types.
problem_solved: There was no standardized way to evaluate LLM expertise on animal-specific scientific and reference knowledge (taxonomy, behavior, distribution, vocalizations, etc.) under a closed-book protocol; BAGEL fills that gap.
method: Assemble a diverse dataset from scientific and reference sources (bioRxiv, Global Biotic Interactions, Xeno-canto, Wikipedia).
Create closed-book question–answer items via a combination of automated extraction and manual curation to cover taxonomy, behavior, distribution, and vocalization knowledge.
Evaluate multiple LLMs under a consistent closed-book protocol to quantify accuracy and identify domain-specific strengths and weaknesses.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a focused benchmark to diagnose and improve LLM performance on ecological and biological tasks, guiding dataset augmentation, fine-tuning, and deployment decisions in conservation and bioinformatics applications.
visual_elements: Source icons map showing dataset provenance (bioRxiv, Global Biotic Interactions, Xeno-canto, Wikipedia).
Pipeline diagram: Data collection → curation → closed-book QA construction → model evaluation.
Bar chart comparing model accuracy across question types (taxonomy, behavior, distribution, vocalizations).
Heatmap highlighting knowledge gaps across taxonomic groups (birds, mammals, insects, etc.).
paper_title: BAGEL: Benchmarking Animal Knowledge Expertise in Language Models
paper_authors: Jiacheng Shen, Masato Hagiwara, Milad Alizadeh, Ellen Gilsenan-McMahon, Marius Miron
